title: Bram and the Compass
premise: Astrid Montrose, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate's cheerful enforcers, follows a freak low tide into a sea cave on the Cornish coast and finds the wreck of the Peregrine—and a brass compass that points not north but toward whatever its holder most fears losing. The compass is the key to the wreck's cargo of salvaged memories, and both the Syndicate and the salvage fleet want it. Racing six tides against Captain Ilsa Rehn and her dredgers, Astrid learns the compass shows her the one thing she can't outrun: her drowned brother, whose death she survived by choosing herself. In the end she shatters the compass over open water, paying her debt in memory rather than coin, and sails away lighter, poorer, and finally free.
about_author: Tamsin Vane is a former marine cartographer who spent a decade charting coastlines that no longer exist. She writes adventure fiction from a converted lifeboat station, where the tide still dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Chased out of Penzance by the Syndicate's relentlessly polite enforcer Mr. Quill, Astrid takes a storm-chasing contract along the Cornwall coast to buy time. A freak spring tide drains a cove she's never seen accessible, revealing a cave mouth carved with warning glyphs. Emotional beat: restless desperation—the exhaustion of always moving, and the first flicker of curiosity stronger than fear.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wants
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with an interlude from Captain Rehn. Inside the cave, Astrid finds the Peregrine's hold and the brass compass; when she grips it, it drags her into a memory of her brother Tomas drowning—her choice to live burned into her. Above, Rehn's salvage fleet anchors offshore, tipped off by Quill. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the compass reveals it feeds on what you refuse to remember.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Astrid and Rehn. Astrid bargains with Quill—the compass for her debt—but discovers the Syndicate plans to harvest the wreck's memory-cargo to sell other people's pasts. Rehn, meanwhile, reveals the compass once belonged to her lost crew, and offers Astrid partnership. Betrayed by both sides, Astrid steals a skiff as the third tide turns. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing every rescuer has a price list.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cornered at the wreck during the final storm tide, Astrid lets the compass show her everything—Tomas's last moments, her own survival, Rehn's grief—until the truth stops being a weapon. She breaks the compass over the rail, releasing the memories back to the sea, and Quill's claim dissolves with the cargo. Rehn lets her go. Emotional beat: grief accepted at last; survival redefined as something you carry, not flee.
